Source: Fermilab Survey, Alignment and Geodesy group (Virgil Bocean), note addressed to Luke
(Corwin), forwarded by A. Norman on 2026-11-05.  Transcribed verbatim from the email.

Hi Luke,

Please find attached the NOvA Far Detector Upstream Face Center coordinates in the beamline system with the following axes orientation:

Origin = MCZERO
X = positive beam right (Eastward) when looking downstream beamline
Y (stationing) = positive downstream beamline
Z = positive upward when looking downstream beamline (and orthogonal to the beam)

                                                   X [m]                     Y [m]                   Z [m]
NOvA_FD_ UPST_Face_CTR     -11037.455993      810422.323775      -4162.644422

The point was computed as it follows:
-          7.5" from where the midline of the rails intersects the wall, to account for the metal bookend between the wall and the detector
-          Vertically, starting from the measured highest floor point which had an elevation in the national NAVD88 vertical datum of H=1181.8175 ft
(point used for calculating shims thickness under the supporting pallets throughout the Detector Hall), we accounted for 23.25" the height of
the pallet and the 304.21" half size of the detector plane; The resulted elevation for the center of the detector upstream face is H = 1209.1058 ft.

Please let me know if more detail and/or information are needed.

Thanks.

Virgil
